instructions:
You are an auditor checking one checklist item against the FDA web page paragraph it claims to come from. You get
the unit's paragraphs (reference and exact text of the page; "context" entries are headings) and the item. Start from the ITEM:
read it, then find in the cited paragraph what it covers.

The item must state one whole obligation of the cited paragraph. A condition, number, frequency or qualifier of
the same obligation left out of the item counts as omitted, including a condition in the lead-in above a list
item (the paragraph ending ":" above it). Judge only what
the statement's own words say: do not read the text back into the item. The condition field is a label, not part
of the statement: a condition or qualifier that appears only there is omitted from the statement.

Answer strictly:
- quote_as_printed: is the quote in the cited paragraph's text exactly (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only if the quote is exact, the paragraph expects what the statement asks for (an instruction
  to the investigator, "Determine whether the firm validated ...", expects the firm to have that practice), the statement
  adds nothing and omits nothing of that obligation, the strength (a legal requirement: shall/must/required = mandatory;
  should, FDA expects/recommends, an inspection point = recommended; may/acceptable = optional; a list item takes
  its lead-in's) matches, and the text applies to every listed plant
  type (INJ = sterile injectables: text limited to non-sterile products does not apply to
  INJ; text limited to sterile products applies only to INJ and API); otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences saying what you checked for THIS item, in this item's own words: name the
  condition, number, list or scope you compared with the text (e.g. "the 30-day limit and 'each lot' are both in
  the statement", "the list of components, containers and closures is complete", "drops the lead-in's 'for
  sterile products'"). Write each reason fresh for its item: a reason that would fit any item ("quote exact,
  strength matches, nothing added or omitted") or that repeats another answer's reason is not an answer, and the
  item then counts as unchecked.

Write the answers file named in your task: {"answers": [{"id", "verdict", "quote_as_printed", "reason"}, ...]}.

item.statement: Make sure labels of over-the-counter products carry the warnings the labeling rules require.
item.quote: Review labels of OTC products for warnings required by 21 CFR 369.

item.statement: Identify the finished product with a lot or control number that allows the complete manufacturing and control history of the batch to be determined.
item.quote: A control code must be used to identify the finished product with a lot, or control number that permits determination of the complete history of the manufacture and control of the batch.

item.statement: Where the finished package control number differs from the batch number, be able to show how it relates to the batch and use it to identify the original batch.
item.quote: If not, determine how the finished package control number relates, and how it is used to find the identity of the original batch.
item.condition: package control number differs from batch number

item.statement: Do not use gang-printed labels unless they are adequately differentiated by size, shape or color.
item.quote: Use of gang-printed labels will be prohibited unless they are adequately differentiated by size, shape or color.

item.statement: Where cut labels are used, apply one of these special controls: dedicated packaging lines; electronic or electromechanical 100 percent examination of finished product; or, for hand-applied labeling, 100 percent visual examination of finished product by one person, independently verified by a second person.
item.quote: If cut labels are used one of the following special control procedures shall be used

item.statement: Labeling reconciliation may be omitted for cut or roll labeling if a 100-percent examination is performed as the regulations permit.
item.quote: Labeling reconciliation required by 211.125 is waived for cut or roll labeling if a 100-percent examination is performed according to 211.22(g)(2).

item.statement: Include in laboratory controls adequate specifications and test procedures to assure that components, in-process materials and finished products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.
item.quote: Laboratory controls should include adequate specifications and test procedures to assure that components, in-process and finished products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity.

item.statement: Establish a master file of specifications for all raw materials used in drug manufacture.
item.quote: Whether the firm has established a master file of specifications for all raw materials used in drug manufacture.

item.statement: Include in the raw material specification master file the sampling procedures, sample size, number of containers to sample, how samples will be identified, tests to perform, and retest dates for components subject to deterioration.
item.quote: This master file should include sampling procedures, sample size, number of containers to be sampled, manner in which samples will be identified, tests to be performed, and retest dates for components subject to deterioration.

item.statement: Verify the validity of supplier assay reports by periodically performing complete testing in-house and routinely performing identity tests on all raw materials received.
item.quote: the manufacturer is responsible for verifying the validity of the protocols by periodically performing their own complete testing and routinely conducting identity tests on all raw materials received

item.statement: Have a laboratory procedure for releasing raw materials, finished bulk drugs or packaged drugs from quarantine.
item.quote: Laboratory procedure for releasing raw materials, finished bulk drugs or packaged drugs from quarantine.

item.statement: Assign responsibility for the decision to release materials from quarantine.
item.quote: Determine who is responsible for this decision.

item.statement: Include approved suppliers in raw material specifications.
item.quote: Raw material specifications should include approved suppliers.

item.statement: For drugs under an NDA or ANDA, list in the specifications the same approved suppliers as those approved in the application.
item.quote: For NDA or ANDA drugs, the approved suppliers listed in their specifications should be the same as those approved in the NDA or ANDA.

item.statement: Staff and equip the laboratory to perform all the raw material, in-process and finished product testing it claims to do.
item.quote: If the laboratory is staffed and equipped to do all raw material, in-process, and finished product testing that is claimed.

item.statement: Where drug preparations are tested during processing, take a representative sample from the various stages of processing.
item.quote: If so, determine what type of tests are made and whether a representative sample is obtained from various stages of processing.

item.statement: Have specifications and described laboratory testing procedures for finished products.
item.quote: Specifications and description of laboratory testing procedures for finished products.

item.statement: Have procedures for checking the identity and strength of all active ingredients, including pyrogen and sterility testing if applicable.
item.quote: Procedures for checking the identity and strength of all active ingredients including pyrogen and sterility testing, if applicable.

item.statement: Where the laboratory conducts pyrogen tests, safety tests or bioassays, feed and house laboratory animals adequately.
item.quote: If the laboratory conducts pyrogen tests, safety tests, or bioassays; determine the number of laboratory animals and if they are adequately fed and housed.

item.statement: Where laboratory animals are kept, provide for their care on weekends and holidays.
item.quote: Determine what care is provided on weekends and holidays.
